# Welcome to QuantLab

**QuantLab** is a network bringing together social scientists at the [University of Melbourne](https://arts.unimelb.edu.au/school-of-social-and-political-sciences) and beyond to share insights in quantitative methods and research.

Co-founded by [Seraphine F. Maerz](https://seraphinem.github.io) (Political Science) and [Irma Mooi-Reci](https://irmamooireci.com/) (Sociology), QuantLab is an inclusive network that welcomes everyone — from students to established researchers — interested in learning about quantitative methods and computational techniques.

Our research is organised into three streams:

- **Political Communication and Computational Discourse Analysis** — led by [Seraphine F. Maerz](https://seraphinem.github.io)
- **Computational Approaches to Workforce Mobility and Inequality** — led by [Irma Mooi-Reci](https://irmamooireci.com/)
- **Computational Literary Studies** — led by [Michael Falk](https://findanexpert.unimelb.edu.au/profile/1043380-michael-falk)

**News:** QuantLab is transitioning into a **Tier 2 research group** at the Faculty of Arts, with [Michael Falk](https://findanexpert.unimelb.edu.au/profile/1043380-michael-falk) (Digital Studies) joining as stream leader and [René Rejón](https://findanexpert.unimelb.edu.au/profile/836491-rene-rejon) (Faculty of Arts) as Outreach and Impact Lead.

We offer hands-on seminars where you can learn cutting-edge methods, together with [free online tutorials and session materials in our Sharezone](sharezone/index.qmd) — step-by-step guides on data management, reproducible research, and ready-to-use scripts in R, Stata, and Python. Most importantly, we provide a space to connect with fellow students and researchers, share ideas as well as knowledge, and collaborate.

:::

# Events in 2026 {#sec-schedule2026}

## AI in Research – Brown Bag Workshop Series

A new collaboration between the [Melbourne Data Analytics Platform (MDAP)](https://www.unimelb.edu.au/mdap), **QuantLab**, and the **Community of AI in Research (CAIR)**. These monthly lunchtime workshops offer a relaxed, hands-on space to build confidence with AI in research — each session runs from 12–1pm at Melbourne Connect, with an optional drop-in until 1.30pm. Bring your lunch, your laptop, and your curiosity. Open to researchers at all levels and across all disciplines.

**[Register and find full details via the MDAP announcement](https://www.unimelb.edu.au/mdap/news/introducing-ai-in-research-brown-bag-series!)** — see also the [series flyer](sessions/AI_BrownBag_2026.pdf).

|:--------:|:------|:----------|
